mesh3d_boundary_patch_guard.interpretation: Mesh3D boundary patches are now classified from the actual domain bounding box instead of hard-coded unit coordinates. This fixes Candido boundary-current decomposition on the stretched cone-jet smoke box.

candido_contact_angle_diagnostic.interpretation: The normal-projection primitive is verified on Candido wall-adjacent mixed cells, but production curvature reconstruction is still unwired.

candido_contact_angle_curvature_diagnost.interpretation: The optional contact-angle local-PIC curvature path affects every wall-adjacent mixed cell without fallback, but it increases stencil condition; it is therefore retained as a diagnostic path until dynamic/static regressions justify production enforcement.

candido_contact_angle_curvature_switch_d.interpretation: The opt-in switch exercises the production CSF loop and remains bounded, but it changes the force scale substantially; default production remains off until static/dynamic surface-tension gates are rerun with this option.

candido_contact_angle_force_decompositio.interpretation: The CSF force-scale drop under contact-angle curvature is explained primarily by the wall-near curvature redistribution: wall mean/max |kappa| fall while the global max |kappa| rises elsewhere.

candido_moderate_vof_compression_morphol.basis: local compression sweep showed 0.06 is the smallest tested moderate compression that keeps mass/divergence bounded while moving fixed-time alpha-integral morphology inside the 10% bar
candido_moderate_vof_compression_morphol.remaining_limits: This upgrades only the coarse alpha-integral morphology proxy. It does not provide missing 0.8/0.9 ms external contour data and does not prove a paper-faithful connected alpha=0.5 silhouette extractor.

morphology_observable_status.current_observable: cell-volume integral of alpha reported in inner-diameter cubed units
morphology_observable_status.paper_observable: axisymmetric alpha=0.5 free-surface silhouette volume V=sum(pi*x^2) along y from nozzle to tip

disconnected_proxy_percent_of_reference.interpretation: After the moderate VOF-compression change, the fixed-time alpha-integral morphology proxy is inside the 10% bar. The disconnected-volume diagnostic remains useful decomposition evidence, not a replacement for the paper alpha=0.5 silhouette.

all_liquid_ray_alpha05_diagnostic_errors.interpretation: Removing the inlet-connected component mask does not recover the Candido Fig. 3(b) silhouette. It overexpands the 0.4 ms fixed-time alpha=0.5 volume and still misses 0.7 ms, so the morphology gap is not a component-filter artifact.

morphology_observable_status.required_next_input_or_method: connected-component PLIC/free-surface intersection with robust cone/jet filtering, or paper-resolution mesh plus independent contour-coordinate digitization

candido_time_alignment_diagnostic.interpretation: This is a timing/observable diagnostic only: the fixed-time alpha-integral volume now falls inside the 10% bar after moderate VOF compression, and best-volume time alignment is closer still. The observable is still not a paper-faithful alpha=0.5 silhouette volume.

candido_morphology_phase_lag_diagnostic.interpretation: Additive root-cause evidence only. It shows that the previous marginal 0.4 ms fixed-time morphology miss was sensitive to interface compression and coarse smoke evolution speed. The alpha-integral proxy is now inside 10%, while the paper-faithful alpha=0.5 silhouette and late 0.8/0.9 references remain unresolved.

candido_ray_alpha05_silhouette_diagnosti.interpretation: The connected ray-sampled alpha=0.5 silhouette is a stricter paper-style observable than the alpha-integral proxy, but on the current coarse smoke mesh it still misses the 0.4 ms digitized reference by slightly more than 10%.

candido_linear_ray_alpha05_silhouette_di.source: least-squares alpha gradient with cell-support ray intersections from the discrete alpha field
candido_linear_ray_alpha05_silhouette_di.interpretation: This additive diagnostic tests whether centroid-only ray sampling caused the alpha=0.5 silhouette miss. It does not improve the paper comparison; the linear-gradient ray reconstruction underestimates the long-window silhouette more strongly, so it is retained as negative evidence rather than a pass path.

candido_ray_alpha05_cell_boundary_silhou.source: connected alpha>=0.5 ray support using outer cell-boundary radius from the discrete alpha field
candido_ray_alpha05_cell_boundary_silhou.interpretation: The cell-boundary support diagnostic tests whether the ray-alpha05 failure is merely cell-center underestimation. It overexpands both digitized comparison frames, so a simple outer-cell correction is not a paper-faithful contour extractor.

candido_morphology_silhouette_bracket_di.interpretation: This additive diagnostic does not clear the paper silhouette gate. After moderate VOF compression, both post-initial digitized references are bracketed by coarse observables, while the paper-faithful connected alpha=0.5 contour extractor remains approximate.

candido_plic_contour_silhouette_diagnost.source: connected reconstructed PLIC interface centroids from discrete alpha
candido_plic_contour_silhouette_diagnost.interpretation: This is negative evidence. The current centroid-only PLIC contour is not a paper-faithful alpha=0.5 silhouette extractor; a clipped interface-polygon/free-surface contour reconstruction is required before morphology can be upgraded.

candido_plic_polygon_silhouette_diagnost.source: connected PLIC plane/cell-edge intersection points from discrete alpha
candido_plic_polygon_silhouette_diagnost.interpretation: This is negative evidence. The clipped plane-edge points are valid interface geometry samples, but using their coarse radial envelope is not equivalent to the paper's morphology volume; the next extractor needs connected outer-contour tracing, nozzle/wall masking, and disconnected-structure rejection.

candido_plic_ray_plane_silhouette_diagno.source: connected PLIC plane/ray intersections with sector-median cut-point comparison
candido_plic_ray_plane_silhouette_diagno.interpretation: Direct PLIC ray-plane contouring is much less overexpanded than raw cut-point envelopes, but it still misses the digitized Candido morphology by more than the 10% bar on the coarse smoke mesh.

candido_plic_first_exit_silhouette_diagn.source: connected PLIC plane/ray intersections using the first outward crossing from the nozzle axis
candido_plic_first_exit_silhouette_diagn.interpretation: The first-exit connected PLIC contour clears the 10% bar at 0.4 ms but severely underestimates the 0.7 ms silhouette. This narrows the morphology blocker to time-evolving connected-contour selection rather than a simple median-vs-first local crossing rule.

candido_plic_ray_plane_q25_silhouette_di.source: connected PLIC plane/ray intersections using an interpolated 25% crossing quantile
candido_plic_ray_plane_q25_silhouette_di.interpretation: Interpolating the lower PLIC ray-plane quantile improves the 0.4 ms silhouette to within the 10% bar, but 0.7 ms remains too small. The morphology gap is not solved by a fixed local crossing quantile.

dynamic_droplet_negated_kappa_force_isol.interpretation: Negating local PLIC kappa restores the restoring-force sign on several rows but leaves order-one or larger acceleration magnitude errors, so a production sign flip is not sufficient.

dynamic_droplet_curvature_mode_diagnosti.interpretation: The local PLIC curvature perturbation has the wrong sign before force assembly. Diagnostic negation restores sign but leaves 45%--75% curvature-coefficient error. A direct local height-quadric fit restores sign without manual negation but has very high stencil condition and remains too weak, so it is diagnostic evidence rather than a production replacement.

dynamic_droplet_cell_grad_force_diagnost.interpretation: A non-production cell-centered sigma*kappa*grad(alpha) diagnostic transfers the same local kappa to acceleration much closer to Lamb than the production balanced-face force, especially for mode-2 n=12. The balanced pressure-gradient path is nearly identical to raw balanced-face CSF, so the blocker is not only the pressure solve. A diagnostic face-Gauss alpha_f*Sf transfer restores the force sign and nearly matches cell-grad magnitude for mode-2, but remains approximate and is not yet a balanced-force production replacement. Projecting the face-Gauss source back through the snGrad pressure operator preserves the restoring sign but weakens the modal force to mode-2 66.0427% and mode-3 86.6535% error, so a simple snGrad projection is not enough.

static_droplet_csf_transfer_diagnostic.interpretation: The face-Gauss alpha_f*Sf transfer is useful as a dynamic modal diagnostic but destroys the static balanced-force cancellation against the snGrad pressure gradient. Paired with a Green-Gauss pressure gradient, the same face-Gauss force balances at machine level, proving the issue is operator pairing. Because the project invariant currently requires identical snGrad for pressure/surface tension, this is design evidence rather than a production promotion.

candido_tip_sync_morphology_diagnostic.interpretation: The standalone long-window budget fixture now regenerates the tip-synchronized morphology diagnostic, so the gap metric no longer depends on a stale full-suite CSV. The alpha-integral volume proxy is within 10% at the synchronized 0.4/0.7 ms paper times, but both all-liquid alpha=0.5 ray diagnostics remain -100%, proving the coarse long-window interface is still not a paper-faithful visible silhouette.

candido_interface_preservation_candidate.method: opt-in conservative post-advection alpha sharpening in the VoF transport path; production default remains zero
candido_interface_preservation_candidate.interpretation: A simple conservative post-advection sharpening is not enough. It partially restores an alpha=0.5 contour at the synchronized 0.4 ms comparison but loses the 0.7 ms contour and worsens the alpha-integral morphology errors. A prescribed nozzle-inflow boundary alpha is more physically faithful and prevents complete alpha=0.5 contour loss at both synchronized times, but it overfills the alpha-integral morphology and still misses the paper silhouette by about 55%. Increasing geometric compression to 0.2 with prescribed inlet alpha is worse: the alpha=0.5 silhouette disappears again and the alpha-integral morphology undershoots by about 22-24%. The next interface-preservation step should couple boundary alpha with contact-line-aware swept-volume/PLIC transport and contour-time tracking, not promote scalar filtering or stronger compression alone.

candido_late_morphology_blocker.required_input: external digitized Fig. 3(b) contour coordinates or morphology volumes at 0.8 ms and 0.9 ms

audited_sources: Candido public AIP Fig. 3 image asset
local external late-morphology dataset input contract
candido_late_morphology_source_audit.interpretation: The long-window fixture regenerates a machine-readable source audit with seven rows: public AIP Figure 3 image, local PDF Fig. 3 render, local paper text, Guo 2018 figures, the Candido data-availability statement, the local external-data schema, and the public author GitHub interIsoFoamEHD repository. The public and local figure assets expose only the 0.0, 0.4, and 0.7 ms panels. The paper text lists 0.8 and 0.9 ms relative errors but not contour coordinates or morphology volumes; the data-availability statement points to corresponding-author request rather than a public dataset; the Guo source paper does not provide Candido-synchronized late contours; and the public author code repository contains solver/case/image material but no postprocessed Candido Fig. 3(b) 0.8/0.9 ms contour or volume CSV. Therefore morphology_late_0_8_0_9_digitized remains false unless an independent late contour/volume dataset is supplied.

candido_current_scaling_validation.interpretation: The paper-comparable convective current reaches the Ganan-Calvo/Candido current scale only in the developed long-window validation row; short 3-step smoke rows remain out of scale and are retained as early-transient diagnostics. The larger conductive value is only a maximum face-flux diagnostic and is not directly comparable to the paper cross-section current.

candido_current_scaling_standalone.method: short standalone current-scaling rows from actual Candido report fields for the current diagnostic candidates; this proves the metric file is backed by live solver output, not a placeholder
candido_current_scaling_standalone.interpretation: These rows are short-fixture diagnostics for radius/current scaling presence. They do not replace the long-window Ganan-Calvo/Candido current-scale validation row and do not make the voltage-sensitivity claim pass.

candido_jet_current_metrics.method: short standalone jet-radius/current metrics from actual Candido report fields for current diagnostic candidates
candido_jet_current_metrics.interpretation: The short fixture now records real jet-radius/current rows. The radii are finite and stable, but the corresponding current rows remain voltage-sensitive and fixed-plane alpha>=0.5 current remains blocked.

candido_refinement_sweep.method: short three-level 2-step Candido smoke sweep on nx=10/12/14 with real force and jet-radius fields active
candido_refinement_sweep.interpretation: The short sweep proves all refinement levels have active forces and bounded numerics; radius passes the current coarse readiness convergence guard and CSF force improves, but electric-force magnitude is not converged. This is mechanical paper-gap evidence, not a full grid-converged Candido validation.

candido_current_voltage_sensitivity.interpretation: The standalone long-window fixture now regenerates primary paper-current sensitivity rows from live reports. Raw long-window current remains catastrophic and the Ca-independent boundary-advection candidates remain above the <=2 weak-voltage bar, but the long paper-boundary combined-charge candidate reaches tail ratio 1.95942. This closes the mechanical paper_current_voltage_sensitivity_ok check at an approximate weak-current level, not a paper-level Fig. 8(b) validation.

candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_ca_i.method: reuse the existing relaxation-limited, Ca-independent electric-drive, boundary-charge-advection path and report it in the same paper-current sensitivity format
candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_ca_i.interpretation: This opt-in current-voltage candidate is many orders better than the raw long-window path and now falls under the <=2 weak-voltage bar after the moderate compression update. It is not promoted as the paper-current validation path because the alpha05 row remains 0/0 at the fixed plane and the same current-friendly path degrades morphology/whipping.

candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_unit.method: same relaxation-limited, Ca-independent, boundary-charge-advection path, but reduce electricDriveReferenceScale from 3.8 to 1.0
candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_unit.interpretation: Reducing the empirical drive scale lowers absolute currents and gives an axial developed alpha05 ratio just under 2 in the drive-scaling diagnostic, but the standard all-phase paper-current sensitivity ratio worsens to 2.47606. The 0/0 alpha05 current-voltage row remains degenerate, so this is not a paper-current pass.

candido_midplane_current_reach_diagnosti.method: fixed mid-domain alpha>=0.5 liquid-jet current-plane reach audit matching Candido Fig. 8(b)'s cross-section-current definition
candido_midplane_current_reach_diagnosti.interpretation: Extending both low/high CaE runs to 90 coarse steps creates a nonzero low-CaE alpha>=0.5 current section, but the high-CaE run has large liquid-mass drift. This still blocks a defensible Fig. 8(b) average-current comparison on the current coarse smoke fixture and shows that simply running longer is not a valid paper-current fix.

candido_reduced_collector_current_fixtur.method: use the current closest ca-independent boundary-charge current path on a reduced 0.75 mm collector-distance fixture to test whether simply moving the fixed middle current plane upstream makes the alpha>=0.5 current observable non-degenerate
candido_reduced_collector_current_fixtur.interpretation: Moving the fixed current plane upstream by halving the collector distance still does not create a non-degenerate alpha>=0.5 current section; enabling VOF inlet boundary alpha gives the same blocked result. This rules out a simple measurement-plane relocation as the current-validation fix and points back to developed-jet dynamics plus physically specified charge/current boundary treatment.

candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_pape.method: short standalone paper-charge-boundary current candidate reusing the paper-charge low/high CaE smoke pair; writes the Candido all-phase average-current source row and the q_e U dot n alpha05 liquid-jet source row without changing solver numerics
candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_pape.interpretation: The standalone candidate is quantified but weaker than the previous long-suite near-pass: all-phase tail/peak ratios are above the weak bar, and the alpha05 liquid-jet observable is zero-current BLOCKED. This keeps the paper-charge path as diagnostic evidence only, not a Candido Fig. 8(b) validation pass.

candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_pape.method: short standalone fully developed inlet-velocity current candidate reusing the paper-inlet low/high CaE smoke pair; writes the Candido all-phase average-current source row and the q_e U dot n alpha05 liquid-jet source row without changing solver numerics
candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_pape.interpretation: The inlet-velocity candidate is now mechanically quantified in the short fixture, but it is still downgraded: all-phase tail/peak ratios exceed the weak bar, and the alpha05 liquid-jet current is a zero observable. Missing inlet velocity is therefore not sufficient to explain the paper-current gap.

candido_fig8b_current_blocker.method: machine-readable blocker summary for Candido Fig. 8(b) current validation using already-computed current candidates; no extra simulation and no threshold relaxation
candido_fig8b_current_blocker.interpretation: The short standalone fixture documents the blocker without the long Candido suite: both paper and reduced fixed planes are undeveloped for alpha>=0.5 liquid current, and the all-phase current ratios remain above the weak bar. This formally documents that Fig. 8(b) remains blocked on the current coarse smoke fixture rather than being solved by current-plane relocation, inlet alpha, nozzle charge-flux suppression, or fully developed inlet velocity.

candido_current_morphology_whip_pareto.method: additive Pareto audit comparing current sensitivity, fixed-plane development, axial alpha05 current, morphology error, and whipping response for live long-window and short candidate reports
candido_current_morphology_whip_pareto.interpretation: The new Pareto artifact prevents promoting a current-only near pass. The baseline keeps morphology and whipping evidence but has catastrophic current sensitivity; the paper-charge and paper-inlet candidates weaken all-phase current sensitivity but still exceed the axial alpha05 convective current bar, leave the fixed Fig. 8(b) plane undeveloped, and lose the morphology/whipping behavior. This is diagnostic evidence, not a validation pass.

candido_open_boundary_current_diagnostic.method: short standalone Candido smoke pair for the paper-inlet/open-atmosphere current candidate; reports open-boundary liquid flux, fixed Fig. 8(b) plane development, axial alpha05 current, mass, continuity, morphology, and radial-asymmetry guards
candido_open_boundary_current_diagnostic.interpretation: In the short standalone fixture the open-atmosphere option has no measurable boundary liquid flux, keeps the fixed Fig. 8(b) plane undeveloped, and still has axial alpha05 convective current ratio above the weak bar. This is quantified mechanical evidence, not a paper-current validation pass.

candido_moving_collector_boundary_diagno.method: short standalone Candido smoke pair for the paper-inlet/open-atmosphere candidate with the reported moving collector speed us=20 mm/s; reports fixed-plane development, current ratios, mass, continuity, morphology, and asymmetry guards
candido_moving_collector_boundary_diagno.interpretation: Adding the reported collector motion is now covered by the short standalone fixture. It preserves bounded mass and projection residuals, but the fixed Fig. 8(b) plane remains undeveloped and current ratios remain above the weak bar, so collector motion alone is not the local explanation for the Candido current gap.

candido_poisson_face_current_observable_.method: short standalone Candido smoke pairs restore Poisson-face current observable, axial-window, convective-factorization, and velocity-projection diagnostics using the same Poisson face-normal flux fields as the solver
candido_poisson_face_current_observable_.interpretation: The standalone fixture restores seven Poisson-face evidence checks. Face-consistent total current is weakly voltage-sensitive, but alpha05 total is a zero-current observable and is explicitly BLOCKED. Paper-charge convective Poisson-face current remains too voltage-sensitive and the projected-vs-raw diagnostic shows the raw velocity current is equally sensitive, so this is not a Rhie-Chow projection artifact. Inlet/open/moving convective rows are still zero-face-flux blocked.

candido_momentum_source_factorization_di.method: short standalone Candido smoke pairs measure mean absolute y-momentum source terms in the tail developed alpha>=0.5 axial bin, separating electric contribution, CSF contribution, total source, source/rho acceleration, and velocity response without changing solver numerics
candido_momentum_source_factorization_di.interpretation: The standalone diagnostic confirms that the Candido current mismatch tracks electric momentum-source sensitivity rather than CSF or missing developed-window bookkeeping. Paper-charge, inlet-velocity, open-atmosphere, moving-collector, Ca-independent, boundary-advected, and unit-Maxwell rows all have 3/3 low/high developed samples; velocity ratios remain about 1.56-1.65 while electric-source ratios remain about 1.68, and every row is DOWNGRADED_ELECTRIC_SOURCE_DRIVES_VELOCITY_SENSITIVITY. This reduces the mechanical evidence gap but does not solve the paper-level current model.

candido_interface_charge_transport_diagn.method: short standalone Candido smoke pairs compare paper-charge baseline against opt-in interface-localized charge redistribution using the same current window as the paper-current diagnostics
candido_interface_charge_transport_diagn.interpretation: The interface-localized redistribution is active and charge-conservative in the short fixture, but it does not reduce the developed alpha>=0.5 current ratio and leaves morphology/whipping far from paper-level evidence. It is useful negative evidence, not a production current closure.

candido_post_charge_potential_refresh_di.method: short standalone Candido smoke pairs compare paper-charge baseline against an opt-in post-charge phi/E refresh before force/current evaluation
candido_post_charge_potential_refresh_di.interpretation: The refresh is numerically active and finite, but in the short live fixture it only changes the developed alpha>=0.5 current ratio from 2.13024 to 2.13014 while morphology remains poor and whipping/asymmetry remains absent. It is APPROXIMATE diagnostic evidence, not a paper-level current closure.

candido_conductivity_potential_charge_cl.method: short standalone Candido smoke pairs compare paper-charge baseline against an opt-in conductivity-potential charge reconstruction before force/current evaluation
candido_conductivity_potential_charge_cl.interpretation: The conductivity-potential closure slightly reduces the short-fixture developed alpha>=0.5 current ratio from 2.13024 to 2.1234, but the electric-source ratio remains 1.68164 and the charge-budget residual is not conservative. It remains an APPROXIMATE diagnostic, not a defensible paper-level model.

candido_conservative_surface_charge_clos.method: short standalone fixture using the same Candido smoke runner for paper-charge-boundary baseline and an opt-in conservative surface-charge candidate with implicit Ohmic projection, conservative charge bounding, interface-localized redistribution, Poisson-face current/force, and post-charge potential refresh
candido_conservative_surface_charge_clos.interpretation: The conservative surface-charge candidate keeps mass, continuity, implicit Ohmic residual, and charge budget bounded, but it does not reduce the Candido-comparable axial alpha>=0.5 convective-current ratio: 2.13035 versus the baseline 2.13023. This is useful negative evidence. The remaining current gap is not fixed by adding conservative bounding plus interface-localized redistribution around the current smoke-path charge update.

candido_electrode_surface_current_bounda.method: short boundary isolation fixture comparing paper-charge-boundary, nozzle-allowed, collector-only, and opt-in implicit-Ohmic-filtered conductive boundary switches
candido_electrode_surface_current_bounda.interpretation: The default nozzle-allowed and collector-only switches still have exactly zero effect because the default implicit Ohmic charge projection recomputes conductive boundary current independently of the pre-filtered conductiveFlux switches. The new opt-in implicit-Ohmic face-scale path proves equivalent boundary filtering can be wired into the sigma operator and reporting flux: nozzle and lateral fluxes are zeroed in the expected rows, and charge-budget residuals improve to about 1e-2. However, the developed alpha>=0.5 current ratio does not improve (2.132 versus the 2.130 baseline), so the paper current gap is no longer just an unwired boundary switch; it requires a stronger leaky-dielectric surface/electrode charge-current model or electric-source calibration.

candido_interfacial_ohmic_charge_source.method: opt-in diffuse-interface leaky-dielectric source rhoE += dt*(-grad(sigma).E), followed by a potential refresh before force/current evaluation
candido_interfacial_ohmic_charge_source.interpretation: The source is active and bounded on the short Candido fixture, but it worsens the developed alpha>=0.5 current ratio from 2.13023 to 4.70647 and raises the electric-source ratio to 3.68941. This rejects a naive diffuse-volume -grad(sigma).E source as the missing Candido current model; the next candidate must be a conservative surface-current/electrode closure or calibrated electric-stress/current update.

candido_paper_current_development_tradeo.method: compare the stable 52-step paper-inlet/open-atmosphere current candidate against a 90-step continuation with the same physics options
candido_paper_current_development_tradeo.interpretation: Extending the paper-inlet/open-atmosphere candidate from 52 to 90 steps preserves mass and continuity, but the fixed paper current plane remains undeveloped. This shows the immediate blocker is not a mass-failure ceiling in the extended candidate; the coarse fixture and current physics do not create a developed alpha>=0.5 jet at y/Di=4.6875 within the tested window.

candido_preconditioned_current_plane_dia.method: short standalone artificial preconditioned liquid-column current-plane reachability diagnostic using usePreconditionedPaperCurrentJet; this is diagnostic-only and not a simulated Taylor cone-jet validation
candido_preconditioned_current_plane_dia.interpretation: The artificial preconditioned liquid column makes the fixed Fig. 8(b) plane non-degenerate and weakly voltage-sensitive at that plane, but axial alpha05 convective current still exceeds the weak bar and the imposed column is not a simulated cone-jet. This only separates reachability from physics; it does not validate Candido current behavior.

candido_total_current_voltage_sensitivit.interpretation: Adding conductive current to the midplane current observable raises the low-CaE baseline but does not remove the high-CaE long-window blow-up. The voltage-sensitivity failure is therefore a charge/momentum evolution problem, not only a convective-current metric artifact.

candido_current_blowup_diagnostic.interpretation: The current-voltage downgrade is coupled to a long-window high-CaE instability and severe open-domain mass accumulation. A separate open-boundary budget now shows this is not a VoF conservation residual.

candido_long_window_mass_budget.interpretation: The standalone long-window fixture closes the geometric VoF budget for both cases. The high-CaE open-domain liquid growth is even larger on this rerun and is explained by the signed open-boundary liquid flux, so it is boundary/dynamics/current-calibration evidence, not a conservative VoF mass-budget defect.

candido_long_window_charge_budget.interpretation: The low-CaE charge budget closes without clamping. The high-CaE run is dominated by charge clipping and a large post-clamp charge-budget residual, so the current-voltage downgrade is tied to the charge-transport/clamping path rather than only to liquid-volume budget error.

candido_charge_subcycling_diagnostic.interpretation: Short standalone subcycling is quantified but downgraded: with no clamp correction to reduce, four subcycles increase the charge-budget residual and max convective current. It is evidence against subcycling alone as the Candido current fix.

candido_charge_conservative_bounding_dia.interpretation: Opt-in conservative charge bounding closes the standalone high-CaE charge budget relative to the unbounded path while leaving the max convective current essentially unchanged. It is a conservation diagnostic, not a paper-current calibration fix.

candido_charge_combined_bounding_subcycl.interpretation: Combining conservative bounding with four subcycles also closes the charge budget in the short fixture, but it increases max convective current by about 4x. This is quantified negative evidence for current calibration, not a solver pass.

candido_current_voltage_sensitivity_comb.interpretation: The long combined conservative-bounded subcycled charge path reaches the weak current-voltage bar with tail ratio <=2. This reduces the mechanical gap, but it is still only an approximate coarse-smoke current candidate and does not upgrade the primary paper-current claim or the missing late morphology data.

candido_charge_relaxation_diagnostic.interpretation: The opt-in quasi-implicit bulk relaxation sink keeps the charge budget closed but does not reduce the high-CaE current or velocity. The remaining current-voltage blocker is therefore boundary/current scaling and charge-cap behavior, not only missing bulk relaxation.

candido_boundary_current_decomposition.interpretation: The high-CaE current failure is dominated by the nozzle/electrode boundary flux, not lateral leakage or collector current. This makes paper-faithful charge-current boundary conditions and dimensional charge scaling the next current-path work item.

candido_boundary_current_sensitivity.method: pairwise low/high CaE patch-resolved conductive boundary-current sensitivity using live long-window and short candidate reports; diagnostic only, no solver numerics changed
candido_boundary_current_sensitivity.interpretation: The new sensitivity artifact separates a useful but limited fact: paper-charge, inlet/open/moving-collector, and unit-Maxwell candidates make cumulative conductive boundary-current ratios weakly sensitive, with nozzle still the dominant high-CaE patch. That does not close Candido Fig. 8(b), because the comparable convective liquid-jet current remains too voltage-sensitive or zero-face-flux, and the morphology/whipping tradeoff remains documented elsewhere.

candido_nozzle_charge_boundary_diagnosti.interpretation: Crude opt-in nozzle conductive-flux suppression reduces the cumulative nozzle flux but worsens current and velocity. The current path needs a paper-faithful boundary-current model and dimensional scaling, not a simple insulated-nozzle switch.

candido_charge_scale_audit.note: Scale-sanity diagnostic only; it does not establish a calibrated nondimensional-to-SI conversion.
candido_charge_scale_audit.interpretation: The high-CaE charge/current path remains dominated by arbitrary charge caps and clamp corrections many orders above a physical charge scale. Nozzle suppression and bulk relaxation do not fix the scale issue.

candido_charge_unit_consistency.interpretation: A single post-hoc charge-unit factor cannot simultaneously calibrate the current smoke path's integrated charge and current observables to physical scales. The charge-current model itself needs dimensionalization and boundary treatment, not just output rescaling.

candido_electric_property_scaling_audit.interpretation: The Candido smoke path uses normalized electrical conductivities whose relaxation scale is about 1877x slower than the physical liquid relaxation scale. Paper-level current validation needs dimensional electrical-property scaling in the charge update.

candido_dimensional_electrical_scaling_d.interpretation: Opt-in physical conductivity scaling fixes the relaxation timescale but destabilizes the current explicit/clamped charge path. The next implementation needs a stiff conservative charge update and boundary-current model, not just dimensional conductivity values.

candido_dimensional_implicit_bulk_conduc.interpretation: A diagnostic split that treats bulk conduction by local backward-Euler relaxation while retaining boundary conductive flux stabilizes the physical-conductivity smoke run and restores charge-budget closure. It still fails current-scale validation because clamp and current remain strongly above the normalized baseline and no single charge unit calibrates integrated charge and current.

candido_nondim_charge_scale_audit.interpretation: The physically motivated Poisson charge scale makes the low-CaE smoke case plausible but does not calibrate the high-CaE whipping/current path. The remaining blocker is the charge boundary/current model and stiff conservative transport, not a missing scalar output conversion.

candido_rayleigh_charge_limit_diagnostic.method: replace the arbitrary qLimit with Q_Rayleigh/(eps0*E0*d0^2) in the same opt-in bounded/subcycled charge path
candido_rayleigh_charge_limit_diagnostic.interpretation: A physically bounded Rayleigh charge cap reduces the high-CaE current scale by orders of magnitude relative to the arbitrary cap but still misses Candido's weak voltage-sensitivity behavior by many orders. The remaining blocker is a dimensional conservative charge-current model with paper-faithful electrode/nozzle boundary treatment, not only the cap value.

candido_collector_only_boundary_current_.method: after fixing Mesh3D patch labels, keep boundary conductive charge flux only on the collector patch while retaining the Rayleigh cap and bounded/subcycled charge path
candido_collector_only_boundary_current_.interpretation: Collector-only boundary current lowers the high-CaE current scale but does not recover weak voltage sensitivity and worsens single charge-unit consistency. This makes a physically dimensional conservative charge-current boundary model the next blocker, not a simple patch filter.

candido_charge_field_consistency_audit.method: compare rhoE with div(eps*E) reconstructed from the cell-gradient electric field used by current and Maxwell-force diagnostics
candido_charge_field_consistency_audit.interpretation: The symmetric Poisson solve converges, but the least-squares cell-gradient E used by downstream current/force diagnostics is not Gauss-law consistent on the coarse cone-jet mesh. The next implementation should add a Poisson-operator-consistent face-normal electric flux path for conductive current and related force diagnostics.

candido_poisson_face_current_diagnostic.method: use a Poisson-operator-consistent face-normal conductive current in the same Rayleigh-capped bounded/subcycled charge path
candido_poisson_face_current_diagnostic.interpretation: Using the Poisson face stencil for conductive charge flux does not recover Candido's weak current-voltage sensitivity and does not remove the order-one cell-gradient Gauss-law mismatch in downstream diagnostics. It is retained as negative evidence, not a promoted current model.

candido_implicit_ohmic_charge_projection.method: opt-in conservative charge update solving (A_eps + dt*A_sigma) phi = q_star with the symmetric Poisson/Ohmic face operator
candido_implicit_ohmic_charge_projection.interpretation: A runnable implicit Ohmic projection reduces neither the weak-voltage-sensitivity failure nor the downstream field-consistency problem enough for paper validation. The current blocker is now isolated beyond a raw explicit stiffness issue: paper-faithful electrode/nozzle boundary current physics and face-consistent force/current assembly are still required.

candido_face_consistent_electric_diagnos.method: opt-in Poisson face-normal conductive current plus Maxwell-stress divergence assembled from the same face-normal Poisson field
candido_face_consistent_electric_diagnos.interpretation: Using face-normal Poisson data for both conductive current and Maxwell stress removes most of the high-CaE absolute current blow-up, but it does not reproduce Candido's weak voltage sensitivity because the low-CaE coarse smoke current nearly vanishes. This is a diagnostic improvement, not paper validation; a paper-faithful boundary/current model and a non-degenerate low-CaE jet state remain required.

candido_face_implicit_electric_diagnosti.method: opt-in implicit Ohmic charge projection plus Poisson face-normal Maxwell-stress force
candido_face_implicit_electric_diagnosti.interpretation: The combined implicit-charge and face-Maxwell path reduces the raw voltage-sensitivity ratio by orders of magnitude, but it remains far above the weak-sensitivity bar and loses the high-CaE developed axial current window. Existing diagnostic pieces are not sufficient; the next current work needs a physical charge-injection/boundary model and developed jet dynamics.

candido_electric_relaxation_timestep_dia.method: opt-in dimensional electrical scaling plus phase electric-relaxation timestep limit on the face-implicit electric path
candido_electric_relaxation_timestep_dia.interpretation: Applying the physical electric relaxation timestep scale plus bounded global charge conservation nearly closes the weak-voltage-sensitivity observable and keeps the charge budget small. After fixing the implicit Ohmic boundary-convective flux accounting, the live ratio is 3.41126, still above the <=2 bar. The fixed midplane remains undeveloped, but the axial developed-window diagnostic has enough low/high samples and still gives ratios of 2.96558-3.54232, so this is not only a measurement-plane artifact.

candido_boundary_charge_advection_diagno.method: opt-in neutral inflow plus zero-gradient outflow charge advection on the relaxation-limited face-implicit electric path
candido_boundary_charge_advection_diagno.interpretation: Adding the paper-motivated convective charge boundary treatment improves charge-budget bookkeeping but worsens the weak-voltage current ratio from 3.41126 to 3.60075. The axial developed-window ratios remain 2.60454-3.0735 with enough low/high samples. This rules out missing boundary charge advection alone as the Candido current-validation blocker.

candido_liquid_jet_current_diagnostic.method: measure Candido Fig. 8(b)-style cross-section current only inside the liquid jet using alpha-weighted and alpha>=0.5 masks
candido_liquid_jet_current_diagnostic.interpretation: Restricting the current observable to the liquid jet makes the low-CaE fixed-midplane current nearly zero and worsens the voltage-sensitivity ratio. The current blocker is therefore coupled jet development and charge transport, not only raw-current contamination outside the liquid.

candido_developed_jet_current_window_dia.method: count tail-window current samples only when the midplane alpha>=0.5 liquid area exceeds 1e-4 inner-diameter^2
candido_developed_jet_current_window_dia.interpretation: The coarse smoke current-voltage comparison is not a valid paper-level Fig. 8(b) average-current comparison because the low-CaE tail has no developed alpha>=0.5 liquid jet at the measurement plane. The face-consistent electric path removes the high-CaE current blow-up but also leaves no developed current plane. A non-degenerate developed-jet fixture or paper-matched measurement plane/time definition is required.

candido_axial_developed_jet_current_wind.method: for each tail sample, choose the axial y-bin with maximum alpha>=0.5 liquid area and compare current only when that developed area exceeds 1e-4 inner-diameter^2
candido_axial_developed_jet_current_wind.interpretation: The default path still fails current-voltage sensitivity even after moving from a fixed midplane to each sample's most developed axial liquid cross-section, so the blocker is not merely measurement-plane placement. The face-consistent electric path is separately blocked because the high-CaE developed axial section disappears on this coarse diagnostic path.

candido_axial_current_factorization_diag.method: factor the alpha>=0.5 axial developed-section current ratio into area, mean absolute charge, mean absolute axial velocity, and charge-velocity alignment using the same history samples as the current-window diagnostic
candido_axial_current_factorization_diag.interpretation: The original long-window failure is dominated by a huge high/low developed-section charge ratio. After the relaxation-limited conservative charge path, area and charge ratios are near unity, but the high-CaE developed axial velocity remains 3.87434x the low-CaE value, leaving current ratios above the <=2 weak-voltage bar. This shifts the next blocker from charge-budget bookkeeping toward electric-force/momentum calibration and paper-resolution developed-jet dynamics.

candido_axial_total_current_closure_diag.method: extend the axial developed alpha>=0.5 scan with the charge-equation current rho_e*u_y + sigma*E_y while retaining the convective q_e*u_y current used by the paper-current observable
candido_axial_total_current_closure_diag.interpretation: The conductive-inclusive axial total current is weakly voltage-sensitive on several bounded/relaxation-limited diagnostic paths, but its conductive share is near unity. This separates the charge-equation Ohmic current behavior from the paper-style convective current i_e=int q_e U dot n dS, which remains DOWNGRADED/APPROXIMATE and still requires paper-faithful charge-current boundary physics and external current calibration.

candido_electric_drive_scaling_diagnosti.method: compare the legacy empirical electric-drive CaE exponent 1.25 against an opt-in Ca-independent Maxwell-force drive scale on the relaxation-limited conservative charge path
candido_electric_drive_scaling_diagnosti.interpretation: Removing the extra empirical CaE^1.25 multiplier from the Maxwell-force drive reaches the all-phase weak-voltage current bar and makes both low/high developed axial windows non-degenerate. The boundary-advection combination still leaves the axial alpha05 current ratio at 2.06484, and the same current-friendly path degrades morphology/whipping, so it should not be promoted without an external calibration basis and a non-coarse developed-current fixture.

candido_axial_current_threshold_sweep_di.method: sweep the minimum alpha>=0.5 axial developed-section area threshold and recompute tail current ratios for baseline, relaxation-limited, and Ca-independent current paths
candido_axial_current_threshold_sweep_di.interpretation: The best Ca-independent boundary-advection path is close but remains above the <=2 alpha05 convective-current bar across all non-degenerate area thresholds from 0 to 2, so the paper-current mismatch is not closed by threshold tuning. The next lever remains physical electric-force/current calibration and developed-jet dynamics, not measurement cutoff selection.

candido_ca_independent_current_resolutio.method: run the best current diagnostic path, Ca-independent electric drive plus boundary charge advection, on n=10/12/14 smoke grids to test whether the near-miss current ratio is a monotone grid-resolution effect
candido_ca_independent_current_resolutio.interpretation: The n=10 point is close but still under-resolved with only five high-CaE developed samples. The two better-sampled grids do not show monotone convergence toward the <=2 alpha05 convective-current bar: n=12 gives 2.06484 and n=14 worsens to 2.37873. The remaining current mismatch cannot honestly be closed by a coarse-grid resolution claim.

candido_ca_independent_morphology_whippi.method: write the near-pass current path, Ca-independent electric drive plus boundary charge advection, into the existing Candido morphology and whipping diagnostics to check whether it can be promoted as a default
candido_ca_independent_morphology_whippi.interpretation: The Ca-independent boundary-advected path is useful for diagnosing the high-CaE velocity bias, but it is not a production default: it misses the strict current bar, worsens morphology to roughly 30% errors at the paper comparison points, leaves the tip quantized on the coarse grid, and fails to reach the 3D whipping asymmetry threshold.

candido_maxwell_tangential_closure_diagn.method: compare one-step cell-gradient Maxwell force, Poisson face-normal-only Maxwell stress, and an opt-in hybrid stress that uses Poisson-normal plus reconstructed tangential electric field components
candido_maxwell_tangential_closure_diagn.interpretation: The face-normal-only stress is executable and bounded, but the hybrid reconstruction changes the force scale by roughly 3.3x on both Candido voltages. This makes scalar electric-drive tuning a weak path; the next production candidate should reconstruct a validated full-vector face electric field and Maxwell stress rather than relying on normal-only face flux.

candido_face_electric_reconstruction_dia.method: compute Poisson face-normal electric field, cell-gradient tangential electric field, and hybrid Maxwell traction from the same initial Candido potential solve; exclude normal-traction-degenerate faces from traction-ratio statistics and report their count separately
candido_face_electric_reconstruction_dia.interpretation: The current Poisson face-normal-only stress discards a large tangential electric-field component on the Candido smoke mesh. The metric now separates degenerate normal-traction faces from active traction-ratio statistics, so the huge hybrid/normal ratios are not a pure division-by-zero artifact. The next current/whipping work needs a bounded and validated full-vector face electric-field reconstruction before any Maxwell-stress closure can be promoted.

candido_bounded_vector_maxwell_diagnosti.method: opt-in bounded full-vector face Maxwell stress candidate: retain Poisson face-normal electric field and clip reconstructed tangential field with normal-field floor fraction 0.05 over limit factors 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, and 2
candido_bounded_vector_maxwell_diagnosti.interpretation: The short force-scale sweep shows the bounded vector candidate is finite and keeps most tangential faces unclipped at factor 2, but this only proves numerical boundedness. It is not validation until the long-window current, morphology, and whipping diagnostics also improve.

candido_bounded_vector_maxwell_long_wind.method: run the factor-2 bounded face-vector Maxwell stress through the long-window Candido current, morphology, and whipping diagnostics on top of the relaxation-limited conservative charge path
candido_bounded_vector_maxwell_long_wind.interpretation: The bounded vector force candidate reduces the raw tail-current ratio but worsens the developed axial alpha05 current ratio and velocity bias, degrades morphology, and does not trigger the whipping threshold. This rules out simple tangential clipping as the paper-faithful Maxwell/current calibration.

candido_hybrid_maxwell_long_window_diagn.method: run the opt-in hybrid Maxwell stress through the full long-window Candido current/morphology/whipping diagnostics on top of the relaxation-limited conservative charge path
candido_hybrid_maxwell_long_window_diagn.interpretation: The hybrid face-normal plus tangential-cell electric-field stress is bounded, but it worsens the full long-window current ratio and does not recover morphology or whipping. This rules out promoting the simple hybrid stress as the production Candido force closure; a validated face-reconstructed full-vector electric field is still required.

candido_tomar_conducting_surface_force_d.method: opt-in Tomar-style conducting surface-force candidate using the discrete alpha gradient as the smoothed interface delta/normal, WHM electric properties, normal conductive current, and tangential electric field from the initial Candido potential solve
candido_tomar_conducting_surface_force_d.interpretation: The Tomar-like conducting surface-force diagnostic is finite, but it is about 24x stiffer than the current default Candido force and is dominated by the normal conductive-current jump term. This is useful force-path evidence, not a validation pass.

candido_tomar_conducting_long_window_dia.method: run the opt-in Tomar-style conducting surface-force candidate through the long-window Candido current diagnostics on top of the relaxation-limited conservative charge path
candido_tomar_conducting_long_window_dia.interpretation: The Tomar-like production path remains numerically finite and reduces the raw tail-current ratio, but it eliminates the developed alpha>=0.5 axial-current window on the coarse Candido fixture. It cannot be promoted as the paper-current fix without a non-degenerate developed-jet validation mesh and paper-matched charge/current boundary physics.

candido_charge_limit_sensitivity.interpretation: The short standalone fixture is insensitive to qLimit=5/50/500 because no charge clamping occurs. This quantifies the local fixture behavior but does not supersede the older long-window charge-scale risk.

missing_requirements.bulk_charge_conservation: paper-faithful conservative bounded charge transport over the full developed cone-jet window
missing_requirements.current_boundary_treatment: published electrode/nozzle/outlet surface-current boundary closure for the Candido configuration
missing_requirements.voltage_sensitivity: external Fig. 8(b)-consistent q_e U dot n current validation with nonzero developed alpha05 liquid-jet observable

candido_charge_model_reference_gap.interpretation: The charge-model reference gap is now explicit and machine-readable: bulk charge conservation, current boundary treatment, and voltage sensitivity remain documented unresolved requirements rather than hidden omissions.

candido_whipping_diagnostic.interpretation: Using the face-coupled Maxwell-stress source restores positive downstream wave translation and places the max global asymmetry close to Candido Fig. 11. The axial-band peak remains too far downstream, so the result is still approximate rather than paper-level.

paper_gap_metric.note: Updated from live build/benchmark_logs after standalone momentum-source, Poisson-face, charge-closure, open-boundary, moving-collector, paper-current candidate, charge subcycling/limit, charge-reference-gap, preconditioned current-plane, reduced-collector, Fig. 8b blocker, jet-current, current-scaling, refinement, long-window budget/Pareto/development, boundary-current, regenerated tip-sync, regenerated primary current-voltage, long combined current-voltage, long paper-boundary combined-current, and late morphology source-audit fixtures; this is targeted evidence, not a full long Candido-suite rerun.

candido_late_morphology_external_dataset.latest_public_reaudit: silviomcandido/interIsoFoamEHD checked; no Candido Fig. 3(b) 0.8/0.9 ms reference contour or volume CSV found
candido_late_morphology_external_dataset.interpretation: The request package makes the remaining external-data requirement actionable without changing the paper-gap truth: empty templates are guarded, reported-error backsolves remain rejected, and the gate stays blocked until independent 0.8/0.9 ms volume or contour data are supplied.
